shareValue: A mobile feature filter builders can use before copying desktop workflows.
caption:
Deploy Studio got approved by Apple today.

I built it because the official App Store Connect app can tell you a build exists, but it still cannot finish the release from your phone. The last mile of shipping was still chained to a desk.

This one is for the odd little moments where the build is ready and you are not at your Mac.

#buildinpublic #indiedev #iosdev #appstore

slides.text: Shipping an app still tied the final step to a desk.
slides.kicker: I could check a build from my phone. I still couldn't finish the release.

slides.text: My first instinct was to put everything on a smaller screen.
slides.kicker: That would have made a mobile copy of a desktop workflow.

slides.text: The breakthrough came when I stopped showing everything.
slides.kicker: Show the one thing blocking the release. Hide what doesn't change the decision.

slides.text: The product became smaller. And much more useful.
slides.kicker: Removing features was harder than building them.

items: Is this urgent away from a desk?
Does it change the next decision?
Can it finish in under a minute?

captions.instagram:
Apple approved the smaller version.

Deploy Studio began as an attempt to carry the whole release workflow onto a phone. That made the product crowded before it was useful.

The turning point was one question: what is blocking this release right now? Everything that did not help answer it became optional—or disappeared.

A mobile tool does not need to be a desktop app squeezed into your hand. Send the last slide to someone shrinking a desktop workflow.

What did your product improve after you removed something?
